passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Ada Lovelace (1815–1852) was an English mathematician.
• She wrote detailed notes on Charles Babbage's proposed Analytical Engine.
• Her notes included an algorithm for computing Bernoulli numbers.
• This algorithm is often regarded as one of the first computer programs.
stem: The student wants to emphasize the significance of Lovelace's notes. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Lovelace's notes on Babbage's Analytical Engine included an algorithm for computing Bernoulli numbers, which is often regarded as one of the first computer programs.
Ada Lovelace, an English mathematician who lived from 1815 to 1852, wrote detailed notes about a calculating machine proposed by Charles Babbage.
Charles Babbage proposed a calculating machine called the Analytical Engine, and the English mathematician Ada Lovelace wrote notes about it.
Lovelace was an English mathematician who wrote notes about a machine, and those notes contained an algorithm for computing a set of numbers.
explanation: The goal is significance. Only A says what the notes contained and why that matters (one of the first computer programs).
source: Emir original item, written to the College Board Digital SAT content specifications
steps: The goal is to emphasize significance.
Significance needs what the notes contained and why it matters.
Only the choice saying the algorithm "is often regarded as one of the first computer programs" explains why the notes matter.
The other choices are accurate but only describe who she was or what she wrote, not why it was important.
key: Rhetorical Synthesis: pick the choice that achieves the stated goal, not just one that is true.
